# Conduct and Confidentiality
Everything in the office staff handbook applies to you as well. Be professional, keep to your uniform and treat your colleagues with respect. Research staff are held to a higher standard of confidentiality, which is set out below.
## Need to know The Company shares information on a need-to-know basis. You'll be told what you need for the work you're doing, and nothing more. That isn't a reflection on you. It's how we protect our people and our research. - Only discuss a project with people who are working on it. - Don't ask colleagues about projects you aren't part of. - Don't share restricted material with other Company staff unless the Lead Researcher has cleared them. - Never discuss your work with anyone outside the Company, whatever they claim to know.
## Classified material Some Company research is classified above your clearance. If you come across a document, sample or data file you weren't meant to see: 1. Stop reading. 2. Don't copy it or tell anyone what it said. 3. Secure it where you found it, or hand it to the Lead Researcher. 4. Report it to the Lead Researcher straight away.
You won't be in trouble for reporting it. You will be if you don't.
## Speaking to outsiders If a colonist, official, journalist or anyone else asks about the lab, say you can't comment and refer them to the Corporate Liaison. Don't confirm or deny anything, even if they seem to know already.
## Ethics The Company is committed to responsible research. If you're asked to do something that worries you, raise it with the Lead Researcher. If your concern is about the Lead Researcher, raise it with the Corporate Liaison.
